items.note: Labconco console brochure (ThermoFisher-hosted, snapshot 691692592182d153) and CSD facility page (57cb108a26a77385) mention automatic/manual collector cool-down start-up modes but state no collector cool-down duration; web search of resellers and user-manual listings found no stated time.

Linkam DSC600 spec/product pages (a20db5c7a7727df9, 7e687738e66ea0c5) give only rates (up to 130 C/min) and range (< -195 C with LNP); no stated time from ambient to base. A time computed from the rate would be an estimate, so none reported.
LTS120 specification page (7aa0f7a55ee6b9c1) gives max heating/cooling rate 30 C/min and response time, but no cool-down time to the minimum temperature; web search found none.
THMSG600 page (f3096c742ac0b54f) gives LNP96 cooling rates 0.01-150 C/min only; no stated cool-down time from ambient to base.

Messer metal cryogenic treatment brochure (34b04ca6ca03867e) gives treatment durations (24 to 72 hours; 1-2 hours sub-zero) which are soak/process times, not a cabinet pull-down time; no pull-down spec found.

NESLAB RTE manual (37e8bb5cdb3964d6) and RTE/EX brochures (901651114fae205b, 30e4ad282600f168) give 'Time to Temperature' / performance curves only as graphs; no numeric pull-down time is stated in text, and reading the curve would be an estimate.
Planer Kryo 560-16 datasheet (d0b214c6e99c2894) gives range +30 to -180 C and cooling rates -0.01 to -50 C/min, start above ambient; no stated chamber pull-down time to a start/hold temperature.

items.quote: Typical mean grinding time | 10 min / 4 min (cooling / grinding)
items.note: RETSCH states a typical pre-cooling phase of 10 min (with LN2 autofill) before 4 min grinding. It is a typical value, not a guaranteed maximum.

MM 400 CryoKit: steel jars are pre-cooled manually by the user in a liquid nitrogen bath (snapshot c7591d067d40187a: 'Steel jars can be precooled manually in liquid nitrogen'); the mill has no cooldown of its own. The page's application text says the sample is sufficiently cooled after approximately 2 minutes in LN2, which is a user embrittlement step rather than a machine cooldown spec.
Sample is cooled by a user-prepared Dewar of cryogen placed on the sample stand (app note 136, snapshot 9f777cd399cdabb7); passive LN2 bath with no machine cooldown spec.
INRIM laboratory page (0acd2ba23c89a0ef) states the PJVS is cooled to 4.2 K in a liquid-helium cryostat but gives no cool-down time.
Lake Shore CPX standard LHe configuration: station cooldown 1.25 h, within a 3 h LHe cycle time that also includes a 0.5 h vacuum pump-down (not added here).
